clue.text: Workers' meeting place's been hived off finally

indicators.note: each of the two words has its final letter taken off, so the closing letter of been and of hived is dropped

explanation.surface: A union's meeting hall has been sold off at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off finally' works on both words: BEEN loses N and HIVED loses D, leaving BEE and HIVE side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees gather in their hive, so it is the place where those workers meet.

clue.text: Bouquets and midday meals initially bought for lecturer

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of the other, swapped for it

parts.note: lunches are midday meals

indicators.note: the first letter of bought is used

explanation.surface: Flowers and lunches were bought for a visiting lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunches of flowers are bouquets, so the plural noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Shelling scary monsters is a mistake

indicators.note: the word loses its shell, its outer letters at each end

parts.note: terrors are frightening monsters

explanation.surface: Firing shells at frightening monsters is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake; the two words are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Tavern by church introduces fish sauce

indicators.note: the inn and church take the fish into themselves

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
sole is a flatfish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pub beside a church brings in a fish sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce is the British informal word for cheek or impudence, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of cheeky backchat is rude impudence, which is insolence.

clue.text: SW river that's short and wide for instance

indicators.note: the river's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
ample means wide or roomy

explanation.surface: A south-western river that is short and broad, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example is a noun naming an instance, so the phrase for instance points to it.

clue.text: Stimulating and softly whimsical after I became leader

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for softly

indicators.note: the letter I is shifted to the front of the word, becoming its leading letter

parts.note: something quaint is whimsically old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Once I took charge, things got lively and pleasantly eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A piquant flavour or remark is sharp and stimulating to the palate or mind.

clue.text: Upsetting request Oscar put in to fork out for young escort

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the payment word

parts.note: to fork out is to pay

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upside down, read from bottom up

parts.note: to beg is to request
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone upset by a request to pay for a young escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' suits a down entry, where the word is read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy is a boy attendant, typically escorting a bride at a wedding.

clue.text: What in Calais we'll see when touring European Union?

definitions.text: What in Calais we'll see when touring European Union?

indicators.note: the French word goes round, touring, the union's letters

parts.note: the French for what is que, Calais being a French port
EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: Asks what travellers to Calais will meet when touring the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a long line at the Calais port.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers at the Calais ferry terminal routinely wait in long lines of cars and people.

clue.text: E.g. Sex Pistols on ecstasy, dead dissolute

parts.note: the Sex Pistols are an example of a band, a band
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A punk group high on ecstasy, dead and debauched.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sex Pistols were a British punk band of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained in behaviour, which is dissolute.

clue.text: In committee, these cuts?

indicators.note: the word sits within the run of letters of committee, these

explanation.surface: Asks whether a committee proposes these spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a baby who teethes cuts teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A teething baby is said to be cutting teeth, so cuts with the question mark points to that.

clue.text: Geordie ways to produce geeks?

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE
roads are ways, abbreviated RDS

explanation.surface: Asks how people from Newcastle go about creating geeks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, in north-east England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerds and geeks are both terms for socially awkward enthusiasts, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: King George say in marble — or ballast in cement

indicators.note: the king and the example are placed inside the stone's name

parts.note: agate is a banded stone, and an agate is also a type of playing marble
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a statue of King George is in marble or in mere concrete filler.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the crushed stone or gravel mixed into cement to make concrete, acting as its bulk filler.

clue.text: Real breaks in joint, result of birth defect

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the joint

parts.note: the hip is a joint

indicators.note: the word Real is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes a genuine fracture in a joint, blamed on a defect from birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like a fracture in the surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft upper lip is a congenital condition, the outcome of a defect present at birth.

clue.text: Bather swims across Dee. How far across?

indicators.note: the rearranged bather stretches across, enclosing, the letter
the letters of Bather swim about into a new order

parts.note: Dee is the spelled-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: A bather swims across the River Dee, and someone asks how wide it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swims' turns BATHER into BREATH; 'across' puts D inside it. Dee also looks like the river, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is the width of something, the measure of how far it is from side to side.

clue.text: Good person right set against another? Yes, oddly

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person
another good person is an angel

explanation.surface: A good person is set squarely against another, and someone remarks how odd that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely and oddly are synonyms, both meaning in an unusual or peculiar way.

clue.text: Stiff and unsupple haircut Em's restyled

indicators.note: the letters are given a new style, like a haircut redone

explanation.surface: Em's haircut, restyled, is stiff and inflexible.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheumatic person suffers joint pain and stiffness, so they are stiff and inflexible.

clue.text: Containers confining nuclear explosions

indicators.note: the bags hold the nuclear letter shut inside them

parts.note: bags are containers

explanation.surface: Vessels holding back nuclear blasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangs are loud explosive noises, so explosions in the plural is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Calf, say, runs inside field regularly drinking mother's milk

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the beast

parts.note: a calf is an example of a beast
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: every other letter of field is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A calf runs about a field, regularly suckling its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastfed baby or animal is fed milk directly from its mother's teats.

clue.text: Beagle finally follows most of hunt trail — it's all part of an act

definitions.text: it's all part of an act

indicators.note: the beagle's letter comes after the trail, following it
only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the scent is the trail followed in a hunt

indicators.note: the closing letter of Beagle is the one taken

explanation.surface: A beagle eventually picks up most of the hunt's trail, as part of the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's act is divided into scenes, so a scene is one part of an act.

clue.text: Coarse gravel found in English ground

indicators.note: the word English is ground down, its letters crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Rough gravel turned up in English soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, as on a beach, which is coarse gravel.

clue.text: Form faced with restructuring is a structure for bridge-building etc

indicators.note: the letters of Form faced are restructured, rebuilt into another order

explanation.surface: A form, once restructured, becomes an engineering structure for bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cofferdam is a watertight enclosure pumped dry so piers and foundations can be built in a river.

clue.text: Crack cocaine's related to immorality

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine, with the 's as a link
re means concerning or related to
vice is immorality

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine is linked to moral decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow opening or fissure, which is a crack in rock or a wall.

clue.text: Some digits run up to show perimeters

indicators.note: in a down clue the run letter climbs higher up the word

parts.note: fingers are some of the digits, toes being the others

explanation.surface: Several fingers ran up to point out the boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' gives R (cricket abbreviation); 'up' moves that R higher in FINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fringes are outer edges or borders, so they are perimeters.

clue.text: Fish from Scottish island set to be fried

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

indicators.note: the letters of set are cooked up, like fried food, into a new order

explanation.surface: Fish caught off a Scottish island, ready to be fried.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullets are a family of food fish, both red and grey types, so they are fish.

clue.text: Enormous blokes squatting in derelict semi

indicators.note: the men occupy, squatting inside, the broken-down semi
the word semi is in ruins, its letters in disorder

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Huge men are squatting in a rundown semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense and enormous are synonyms, both meaning extremely large.

clue.text: A relative from French city on the mobile

indicators.note: heard over a mobile phone, the city's name comes across by voice

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone from the city of Nice calls a relative on their mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is said 'neece', just like the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a kinship relation, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: This month everything's set up for use

parts.note: inst (instant) is the old commercial abbreviation for this month
everything is all, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: This month, everything is ready for use.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, for instant, appeared in old business letters: 'your letter of the 5th inst' means this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment is to put it in place and set it up ready for use.

clue.text: A thousand held in fear and wonder, vigilant

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the feeling

parts.note: awe is a feeling of fear mixed with wonder

explanation.surface: A thousand people held in fear and amazement, watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wide awake and alert is vigilant, keeping watch for danger.

clue.text: A bee when their gang has gone off

indicators.note: the letters of their gang have gone off, wandering into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bee appears once its colony has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Bee here is a social meeting, as in a spelling bee or sewing bee, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is a social gathering for shared work or competition, like a quilting bee.

clue.text: Small flat layer from top of freezing tarn

indicators.note: the top, first, letter of freezing is taken

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

explanation.surface: A thin sheet lifted from the surface of a frozen mountain pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake is a small thin flat piece, like a flake of ice or skin.

clue.text: Evacuate out of Greek island

parts.note: ex means out of, as in exit
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An order to get out of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate the bowels is to expel waste, which is to excrete it.

clue.text: On reflection finish with When The Saints or the blues?

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters are read the other way round

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for saints
the end is the finish
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Wonders whether to finish with the jazz standard When The Saints or with a blues number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns SSENDAS around. 'When The Saints Go Marching In' is a jazz standard, which suits the blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues is an idiom for feeling low, so it names sorrow or melancholy.
